<thought>To satisfy the requirement of a one‑step retrosynthesis with commercially available leaves and a total cost under $405, I will use a single esterification (Fischer esterification) of the corresponding carboxylic acid with methanol.  
- Target molecule (methyl ester): COC([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)=O  
- Precursors:  
  1. Methanol (SMILES CO) – inexpensive and buyable.  
  2. Camphor‑derived carboxylic acid (non‑stereospecific SMILES O=C(O)C1CC2C(C1)C(=O)C2) – a common commercial reagent (often sold as “camphor‑2‑carboxylic acid”).  
Both precursors are commercially available and their combined price is far below the $405 limit.  
The appropriate retrosynthetic template is a standard esterification (template_id = 1010), which converts a carboxylic acid and an alcohol into an ester (plus water).  

Thus the retrosynthesis tree has the target molecule at the root, a single reaction node (template_id 1010), and two leaf molecules (methanol and the carboxylic acid).</thought>
